Comment: CloudLab c240g5, U11's worst case on Amazon 300M: the queries are 2M of the base's own vectors, drawn without repetition (scripts/data/sample_queries.py, seed 1), so no run repeats a query and none has any locality. They are drawn on the control node, from the index's page file and its layout map rebuilt from the partitions (sample_queries.py map); their ground truth covers every 1000th of the first 1M (fusion_gt --index). Set the rates from the two worst-case capacities: Rate about 0.6 x C4 (4to8-worst-calibrate-4), RateSteps 60:exactly twice Rate, below C8 (4to8-worst-calibrate-8), the same in every protocol's file. Otherwise experiment.amazon-300m-cloudlab-gpu-4to8-copy-then-flip.json: 4 -> 8 at 90 s under copy-then-flip. The copy outlasts the load (with the QAC queries it flipped 1636-1768 s after the trigger), and the run keeps what it measured. StageTimeout 2h, as there. The rates here are this reservation's, from its capacities of 2026-11-21, C4 1239 and C8 2483, set by hand: Rate 900, 0.73 x C4, and at 60 s 1800, exactly twice that and 0.72 x C8, about the share of C8 the 4 -> 8 runs' step takes (0.76 on Amazon, 0.71 on Wikipedia). Without locality the reads spread evenly, so C8 is twice C4 here, and 0.6 x C4 would leave the scale-out 40% of C8 free.
